cli-auth.title: What happens when you run one AWS CLI command

steps.label: Boto3 or the CLI looks for credentials in order: environment variables, an SSO profile, shared config, then a role
The request is signed with SigV4 and sent to the Regional service endpoint
The service asks IAM: may this principal call this action on this resource?
An Allow returns the response; no Allow, or any explicit Deny, returns AccessDenied
aws sts get-caller-identity confirms which identity you are really using before you build anything
A CloudWatch billing alarm (the metric lives in us-east-1) emails you through SNS when charges pass your threshold

llm-generation.title: How an LLM writes an answer, one token at a time

steps.label: Text is split into tokens (word pieces). Bills, quotas and the context window all count tokens
Token IDs run through the model, which scores every possible next token
Temperature, top-p and top-k decide which candidates may be picked
One token is chosen
It is appended to the input and the loop repeats. The model is stateless: it only sees what is in this request
It stops at end of turn, a stop sequence or maxTokens, and the tokens become text

semantic-search.title: Embed once, search by meaning forever

steps.label: Offline: documents are chunked, embedded and stored once, with their text and metadata
Online: the question is embedded with the same model (mixing models breaks the geometry)
The store finds the nearest vectors by cosine similarity, optionally narrowed by a metadata filter
The top-k chunks go into the prompt next to the question

converse-request.title: One Converse call, end to end

steps.label: converse(modelId, messages, system, inferenceConfig) is signed and sent: one format for most chat models
Bedrock checks IAM, SCPs and your quota before running anything
Over your quota: 429 ThrottlingException. The SDK retries with exponential backoff and jitter, never in a tight loop
The retry is admitted and the model runs inference
Back come output.message, stopReason and usage. The app must resend history next turn: Bedrock is stateless

customization-job.title: From labeled examples to a custom model in production

steps.label: Hundreds of examples of exactly the behavior you want: cleaned, deduplicated, PII-masked, validated as JSONL
Training and validation files go to S3; the customization job reads them with its service role
Training (fine-tuning, distillation or reinforcement fine-tuning) produces a custom model
Option A: Provisioned Throughput for steady, predictable load
Option B: an on-demand custom model deployment, paid per token. Facts that change still belong in RAG
Ingestion (offline): parse, chunk, embed and store. Update knowledge by re-syncing documents, never by retraining
Query (online): optionally rewrite or decompose the question, then embed it with the same model
Semantic or hybrid search returns candidates, narrowed by metadata (department, date, tenant)
A reranker puts the best passages first; the prompt says “answer only from these sources”
The model answers and a contextual grounding check flags claims the sources do not support

kb-retrieve-generate.title: Bedrock Knowledge Bases: Retrieve vs RetrieveAndGenerate

steps.label: A sync (ingestion job) reads S3 and connectors, then parses, chunks and embeds what changed
Bedrock assumes the knowledge base's service role to read sources and call the embedding model
Chunks, vectors and metadata land in the store: managed by AWS, or your OpenSearch, Aurora or Neptune
Retrieve: hybrid search with metadata filters and an optional reranker
…returns chunks with score, source location and metadata. You build the prompt
RetrieveAndGenerate: one call retrieves, prompts the model and returns an answer with citations

rerank-pipeline.title: Over-fetch, rerank, then prove which chunking wins

steps.label: Search over-fetches: 20–50 candidates by vector or hybrid score
A reranker reads the query and each passage together and re-scores relevance
Only the best few reach the prompt: more relevant and cheaper
To choose a chunking strategy, run the same golden questions against each variant
Score retrieval (hit@k, MRR, or a Bedrock RAG evaluation job) and keep the winner

multimodal-pipeline.title: A multimodal pipeline turns messy files into trusted data

steps.label: Raw files land in S3 and are routed by type
Images: resize and redact, then a vision-capable model reads them through Converse
PDFs, forms and video: Bedrock Data Automation returns structured output with confidence scores
Audio: Transcribe to text, then Comprehend or an FM for entities, sentiment and summaries
Every branch is validated: schema, value ranges, confidence
Pass → store it for the rest of the system
Fail or low confidence → a human review queue

guardrail-sequence.title: A guardrail checks both directions of every call

steps.label: The question is evaluated first: content filters, denied topics, word filters, PII, prompt attacks
A violation never reaches the model: the user gets the configured blocked message
Clean (or PII-masked) input is forwarded to the model
The response is checked too: the same policies, plus contextual grounding against the retrieved sources
Allowed, masked or replaced, the final answer goes back. Guardrails reduce risk; they are one layer, not a guarantee

prompt-flow.title: A Bedrock Flow is a flowchart that runs

steps.label: The input flows into a prompt node that rewrites the question; a knowledge base node retrieves
A second prompt node (a versioned prompt from Prompt Management) answers with sources
Conditions are evaluated in order: confidence ≥ 0.8 sends the answer straight out
Otherwise the default branch runs a Lambda node that escalates to a human queue

defense-in-depth.title: Prompt injection is stopped by layers, not by a system prompt

steps.label: Untrusted input passes WAF and input validation, then the Guardrails prompt-attack filter
Text that says “ignore previous instructions” is caught by the prompt-attack filter
The template keeps your instructions apart from tagged, delimited user data
Output is filtered and validated; any action runs under a role that can do only that job
Everything is logged and alarmed: CloudTrail, invocation logs, guardrail traces

genai-gateway.title: A governed GenAI gateway for the whole enterprise

steps.label: Customers (Cognito) and employees (Identity Center) enter through API Gateway behind WAF
Legacy systems integrate loosely, by events through EventBridge or SQS
Every team uses the same gateway: authentication, quotas, then the central guardrail
A config-driven router picks the model and calls Bedrock privately through an interface endpoint
Structured logs, metrics and cost-allocation tags per team make chargeback and audit possible

text-to-sql.title: Numbers come from the database, words from the model

steps.label: “What does the refund policy say?” is a meaning lookup, so it goes to vector search
“Total refunds by region last quarter?” needs counting: a structured knowledge base turns it into SQL
DIY: the model proposes SQL and a validator allows only SELECT on approved tables, with a LIMIT
It runs under a read-only database role. A prompt is not a security boundary
Rows or passages come back and the model explains the result, citing its source

data-wrangler.title: Data Wrangler records every cleaning step as a reusable flow

steps.label: Import a sample, then clean, convert and featurize. Every step is recorded in the flow
The Data Insights and Quality Report flags missing values, duplicates and outliers
Issues found: back to the transforms
Healthy: export the flow
Run the same steps on the full dataset: write to S3, a SageMaker pipeline or Feature Store

glue-dq-gate.title: A data-quality gate in front of the knowledge base

steps.label: A Glue job loads the batch and evaluates the Data Quality ruleset (completeness, uniqueness, row count…)
Score at or above the threshold (score = percentage of rules passed) → clean prefix → ingestion
Below the threshold → quarantine, so bad data never reaches the knowledge base
The result event notifies the team or stops the pipeline
Scores are published as CloudWatch metrics, ready for trend alarms

audio-insights.title: Audio to insight: Transcribe → Comprehend → model

steps.label: An S3 event starts a Transcribe batch job (live captions would use streaming instead)
The transcript JSON, with timestamps and speaker labels, lands in S3 and triggers analysis
Comprehend extracts PII, entities and sentiment; a gate checks confidence and PII handling
Pass → a Bedrock model summarizes the redacted text and the result is stored
Fail → human review. Comprehend extracts; it never generates

opensearch-knn.title: One k-NN query across OpenSearch shards

steps.label: The question is embedded with the ingest model and sent as a knn query
Each shard searches its own HNSW graph and returns its top k: shard sizing drives latency
The coordinating node merges shard results down to `size` (forget it and you get 10)
Optionally rerank, then the best chunks become the model's context

s3-vectors.title: S3 Vectors: pay for storage and queries, not a running cluster

steps.label: Chunks are embedded and written with PutVectors, up to 500 per call, with filterable metadata
A query calls QueryVectors with topK and a metadata filter
Matching chunks and metadata feed the model
A Bedrock knowledge base can use the index as its vector store
Hot, high-QPS data can be exported to OpenSearch Serverless; S3 Vectors keeps the cheap long tail

pgvector-rag.title: pgvector: vectors in the same row as your business data

steps.label: Files are extracted, chunked, embedded and UPSERTed next to the business columns
The app embeds the question
One SQL statement: WHERE customer_id = 42 AND created ≥ 2026 ORDER BY embedding <=> $q LIMIT 5
Rows (chunk, s3_uri, metadata) come back and become the prompt
A Bedrock knowledge base can use the same table through the RDS Data API and a Secrets Manager secret

dynamodb-chat-state.title: DynamoDB holds the state a stateless model needs

steps.label: Load this session's history by key in single-digit milliseconds
Exact-match cache lookup on a hash of the normalized request
Miss: call the model with the trimmed history
Append the turn and token count; store the answer with a TTL (epoch seconds; expiry is not instant)
DynamoDB Streams fans changes out to indexing, metrics and audit

s3-data-protection.title: Five S3 questions for GenAI data: cost, failure, keys, access, audit

steps.label: Each team reaches the shared bucket through its own access point and policy
Every new object is encrypted (SSE-S3 by default); SSE-KMS with a Bucket Key cuts KMS request cost
Replication copies new objects to another Region; versioning is required on both buckets
Lifecycle rules move cold data down the storage classes, ending in Deep Archive
Server access logs record each request, delivered on a best-effort basis

agent-classic-loop.title: An agent loop: reason, act, observe, repeat

steps.label: The agent sends instructions, tool schemas and history to the model
The model chooses an action, getOrderStatus(order_id), and the action-group Lambda runs it
The result is added to the prompt as an observation
Next it decides to search the knowledge base
Passages come back as another observation; iteration limits stop a runaway loop
Enough to answer: the response streams back with a trace of every step

supervisor-agents.title: A supervisor splits the work; memory keeps what matters

steps.label: “Refinance my loan and explain today's new-mortgage rates” spans two specialists
The supervisor splits the request and hands each part to the right collaborator
Each specialist answers only its part, with its own small set of tools
The supervisor merges them into one reply
Turns stay in short-term memory; background extraction distills durable facts into long-term memory

agent-squad-routing.title: Agent Squad routes; Strands agents do the work

steps.label: Requests reach agents hosted in an AgentCore Runtime container: hosting and isolation are not the library's job
Agent Squad classifies each message, using the conversation so far
“Why was I charged twice?” → the billing agent, a Strands agent, runs its loop with the model and its tools
A follow-up about Wi-Fi is routed to the tech-support agent, context kept

agentcore-gateway.title: AgentCore Gateway and Policy: tools with deterministic control

steps.label: The agent authenticates with an OAuth JWT or IAM and lists tools over MCP
Every tool call is checked by Policy outside the agent's code: default deny, forbid wins
Permitted: the call reaches its target
For a SaaS target, Identity supplies the user's delegated OAuth token: the agent never holds the secret
A forbidden call (a refund over the limit) is denied deterministically; no prompt can argue past it
Every step is traced for Observability and scored by online Evaluations

code-vs-config.title: Two ways to ship an agent: code it, or configure it

steps.label: Code path: write the agent with Strands and deploy it to AgentCore Runtime
It runs in an isolated session with Memory and a model
Config path: declare model, prompt, tools, memory and limits. There is no loop to write
The harness (built on Strands) runs the standard loop with your tools; it is the closest replacement for Agents Classic

tool-use-loop.title: Tool use: the model asks, your code acts

steps.label: Send messages plus toolConfig: each tool's name, description and JSON schema
The model cannot run anything: it stops with stopReason tool_use and a toolUse block
Your code validates the arguments and runs the tool (Guardrails do not check tool arguments)
Send back a user message holding toolResult with the same toolUseId
The model writes the final answer
Money, deletion, email: pause for a person first, e.g. a Step Functions task-token callback

mcp-transport.title: MCP: one protocol between any agent and any tool server

steps.label: The host runs one MCP client per server it connects to
Local servers talk over stdio
Remote servers talk Streamable HTTP, hosted on Lambda, ECS or AgentCore Runtime
Each server exposes its tools, resources and prompts the same way
Results come back in one standard format: any agent, any tool

quick-landscape.title: Business users vs developers: who builds the agent?

steps.label: No-code: business users chat, research and automate in Amazon Quick over connected data
Q Apps turn a good prompt into a small shareable card app
Developers build customer-facing agents on AgentCore, with Gateway tools and Memory
…or code the loop themselves with Strands Agents
Everything you send is input: system prompt and tool definitions, history, retrieved chunks, the question
The model writes output tokens, usually the pricier kind
Both are billed and both count against tokens-per-minute quotas
Trim history to a budget, cache the stable prefix, retrieve less, cap maxTokens: same answer, fewer tokens
The edge caches GET responses; a POST chat request goes on to the app
Exact-match cache: a hash of model, prompt, parameters, prompt version and tenant
Semantic cache: a paraphrase above the similarity threshold returns a stored answer
Call Bedrock: an unchanged prefix (system prompt, documents) is read from the prompt cache
Store the answer in the exact and semantic caches, keyed per tenant, with a TTL
Next time, the request stops at the first layer that already knows the answer

latency-pipeline.title: Where the seconds go in one GenAI request

steps.label: Rewrite and retrieval run first; independent calls should run in parallel
The prompt is assembled and the wait for the first token starts
Streaming shows tokens as they arrive, so perceived latency drops even when total time does not
Validation and post-processing finish the answer. Profile every stage before optimizing any

cris-routing.title: Cross-Region inference: more capacity, same API call

steps.label: The app calls a cross-Region inference profile ID from its source Region
Region A is short of capacity…
…so Bedrock routes the request to a destination Region with spare capacity
The response returns to the source Region
CloudTrail and CloudWatch record the call in the source Region
IAM and SCPs must allow every destination Region the profile can use, or calls fail

endpoint-picker.title: Pick the SageMaker AI inference option from the workload

steps.label: Payloads up to 1 GB or up to an hour of processing, and queueing is fine: asynchronous endpoint
Interactive and needs a GPU, a VPC or a large model: real-time endpoint, inference components to share instances
Interactive but idle most of the time, model fits in 6 GB, cold starts acceptable: serverless (no GPUs)
A whole dataset offline: batch transform

model-monitor.title: Model Monitor compares live traffic with a baseline

steps.label: The endpoint captures a sample of requests and responses to S3
A scheduled monitoring job reads the capture…
…and compares it with baseline statistics and constraints (model quality also needs ground-truth labels)
Drift beyond the constraints: a violations report, CloudWatch metrics and an alarm

registry-approval.title: Model Registry: approval status drives deployment

steps.label: Every new version enters its model group as PendingManualApproval
Approving it emits an event and the pipeline deploys it. Approval alone deploys nothing
Rejecting a pending version deploys nothing
Roll back: reject the live version and CI/CD redeploys the latest Approved one

lineage.title: Lineage answers “what trained the model behind this endpoint?”

steps.label: ContributedTo: the data and the container image feed a training job
Produced: the job produces the model artifact
ContributedTo, then AssociatedWith: the package is what the endpoint serves
QueryLineage walks it backwards for an auditor; across accounts, share the lineage group with AWS RAM
Steps run as a graph: process, train, evaluate
A condition step reads the evaluation report
Good enough: register in Model Registry, create the model, run batch predictions
Below the bar: the run ends and nothing is registered

lambda-invocation-modes.title: Three ways Lambda gets invoked, three retry stories

steps.label: Synchronous: the caller waits for the result or the error (default timeout is just 3 s)
Asynchronous: Lambda queues the event and returns 202 at once
Failures are retried; after the retries the event goes to a DLQ or an on-failure destination
Polling: an event source mapping reads batches from SQS or a stream
An error returns the batch for retry; report partial batch failures so good records are not redone

apigw-front-door.title: API Gateway: every check before a model call costs money

steps.label: WAF filters floods and injection patterns before the API ever sees the request
An authorizer verifies the caller, then a validator rejects malformed or oversized bodies cheaply
A usage plan enforces per-client rate, burst and quota; API keys identify, they don't authenticate
Only now does Lambda spend money on a model call
Long answers stream back (REST response streaming) instead of hitting the default 29-second timeout

appconfig-rollout.title: Switch models without a redeploy, and roll back on an alarm

steps.label: Model ID, temperature, prompt version and kill switches live outside the code; validators check every change
A deployment strategy rolls the change out gradually, for example 10% of targets at a time
Functions read the cached value, polled in the background. No redeploy
An alarm fires during the rollout or the bake time…
…and AppConfig rolls the configuration back automatically

prompt-chain.title: A Step Functions prompt chain with a fallback model

steps.label: Draft, then critique: each state calls Bedrock directly, no Lambda in between
Rewrite with the critique and the chain finishes, with every run recorded
If the draft state fails after its Retry, Catch (States.ALL) routes to a fallback model
The fallback draft rejoins the chain
Retries exhausted later on: fail with a clear error instead of hanging

cicd-pipeline.title: Ship a GenAI change only if the golden prompts still pass

steps.label: A commit (code, prompt template or IaC) builds, runs unit tests and the golden prompt set
High-risk changes wait for a person (a pending approval fails after 7 days)
CodeDeploy publishes v8 and a BeforeAllowTraffic hook evaluates it first
Traffic shifts 10%, then 100%, while alarms watch errors, latency and guardrail blocks
An alarm triggers automatic rollback: the alias stays on v7

appsync-subscription.title: AppSync subscriptions deliver a slow AI answer piece by piece

steps.label: 1. The client opens a subscription over WebSocket
2–3. A mutation asks the question and AppSync invokes Lambda asynchronously…
4. …and answers at once, so no resolver hits its timeout
5–6. Lambda calls Bedrock and receives the tokens
7–8. Each update is published as a mutation and pushed to every subscriber

edge-placement.title: Outposts and Wavelength extend a Region; Bedrock stays in it

steps.label: Mobile users reach compute inside the carrier's 5G network in very few hops
Managed Bedrock models stay in the parent Region; the edge forwards what needs a model
On-premises data is processed on Outposts racks right next to it, for residency
Only approved, redacted text crosses the service link to the Region
Guardrails apply in the Region as usual

sns-fanout.title: Fan out with SNS, buffer with SQS, park failures in a DLQ

steps.label: One upload event is published once, to an SNS topic
Fan-out: each subscription's filter policy decides who receives it. SNS pushes; it does not buffer
Queues buffer the work and workers pull at their own pace, so the model never sees the burst
A message that keeps failing moves to the DLQ after maxReceiveCount: alarm, fix, redrive

eval-job.title: A Bedrock evaluation job gates the release

steps.label: A golden dataset drives the job; the generator answers every prompt (or you bring your own responses)
Responses are scored programmatically, by a judge model with a rubric, or by people
Scores and per-item explanations land in a report
The release ships only if it beats the baseline, then canaries before full traffic

rai-lifecycle.title: Responsible AI is a loop, not a launch checklist

steps.label: Assess the risks, design controls, then test fairness, safety and robustness before release
Pass the gate and ship
Runtime controls ship with it: Guardrails, human approval, grounding and citations
Monitor logs, alarms and sampled judge scores; keep the evidence for audits
Every new failure becomes a new test case

cw-observability.title: CloudWatch for a GenAI app: metrics, logs, alarms

steps.label: Bedrock publishes metrics automatically: invocations, latency, tokens, throttles
Model invocation logging is off by default; turn it on to capture every request and response
Logs Insights queries the logs; metric filters turn log patterns into metrics
An alarm (M out of N datapoints) changes state and notifies on-call
Dashboards chart the metrics and log queries, including the ready-made generative AI observability views

cloudtrail-pipeline.title: CloudTrail records the call, never the prompt

steps.label: Every API call is recorded: who called Converse, on which model, when, from where. Not the prompt content
Event history keeps 90 days of management events at no charge
A trail (add data events for agents, KBs, flows) delivers files to S3 with integrity digests for analysis
Matching events can trigger alerts or automatic responses

lake-formation-vending.title: Lake Formation decides which rows and columns a query may see

steps.label: 1. The engine asks the Data Catalog for the table's metadata
2. Lake Formation checks the caller's grants on databases, tables, columns and rows
3. Credential vending: the engine gets short-lived access to only the allowed data
4. It reads S3 and applies the column, row and cell filters
The user (or the agent acting for them) sees only what they could query directly
Grants and data access are audited in CloudTrail

identity-center.title: People federate in; applications assume roles

steps.label: People sign in once through IAM Identity Center (federated, MFA) and choose a permission set
They receive short-lived role credentials, scoped to the approved models
Applications use roles, never stored keys, and mask card numbers and IDs before data reaches a model or a log

org-governance.title: Control Tower: guardrails for a whole organization

steps.label: Control Tower builds a multi-account landing zone on AWS Organizations
Accounts are grouped into organizational units
SCPs and controls on the GenAI OU apply to every account in it, e.g. Bedrock only in two Regions. SCPs never grant
Account Factory vends new accounts with the baseline already applied
Logs flow to a central archive; an organization-enforced guardrail covers every model call
1. GenerateDataKey: ask KMS for a fresh data key
2. KMS returns it twice: in plaintext, and encrypted under the KMS key
3. Encrypt locally with the plaintext key, discard it, store the sealed key beside the data
4. Later: send the sealed data key back to KMS
5. KMS checks the key policy, IAM and grants, then returns the plaintext key
Every KMS call is logged in CloudTrail; rotation creates new key material but does not re-encrypt old data

cognito-waf.title: Cognito knows who the user is; WAF stops what they send

steps.label: Sign in to the user pool and receive ID and access tokens (JWTs)
HTTPS with the access token: WAF screens it first (rate-based rules, managed rules, bots)
API Gateway's Cognito authorizer validates the token; only then is a model called
A flood from one IP passes the rate-based rule's limit and is blocked
Optionally an identity pool trades the ID token for scoped AWS credentials, e.g. one S3 prefix per user

private-bedrock.title: Calling Bedrock without touching the internet

steps.label: Private DNS resolves bedrock-runtime to the interface endpoint's private IP; traffic rides PrivateLink
KMS, Secrets Manager and CloudWatch Logs need interface endpoints too
S3 (and DynamoDB) use free gateway endpoints, a route-table entry. Bedrock has no gateway endpoint
An endpoint policy can restrict which models may be invoked through the endpoint

kinesis-kb-fresh.title: Streams keep a knowledge base fresh and feed analytics

steps.label: Producers write records with a partition key; the key decides the shard
A Lambda consumer calls IngestKnowledgeBaseDocuments, so new tickets are searchable within minutes
Enhanced fan-out gives Flink its own 2 MB/s per shard to write analytics to S3
Athena queries S3 in place; Quick Sight draws the dashboard

contact-center.title: A contact-center assistant: Connect, Lex and Bedrock

steps.label: A call enters a Connect flow and reaches the Lex bot
“Where is order 123?” matches an intent and Lambda fulfills it
Nothing matches: AMAZON.QnAIntent answers from a knowledge base with a guarded model
Still stuck: escalate to a human agent

semantic-cache-graphrag.title: Semantic cache first, GraphRAG when it misses

steps.label: Embed the question and look it up in the semantic cache
Similarity at or above the tuned threshold: return the stored answer
A miss goes to GraphRAG: retrieve chunks, then expand along graph relationships
The multi-hop context goes to the model
The answer is stored with a TTL for the next similar question

cdk-deploy.title: Infrastructure as code for a GenAI stack

steps.label: cdk synth turns code into a CloudFormation template; a change set previews the change (it does not check permissions or quotas)
Execute: the stack creates the guardrail, knowledge base, Lambda functions and roles
Builds log in to CodeArtifact, which fetches approved public packages on demand
Drift detection finds changes someone made by hand in the console

doc-human-review.title: Machines extract; people review what machines are unsure of

steps.label: Textract reads text, forms and tables; Rekognition checks images for unsafe content
Every extraction carries a confidence score
High confidence goes straight through
Low confidence goes to a person first (A2I is closed to new customers; your own queue works too)

autoscaling-loop.title: Scale on the right metric; alert on strange spend

steps.label: Target tracking keeps a metric near its target by adding or removing capacity
Scheduled actions pre-scale for peaks you know about
Cost Anomaly Detection spots an agent stuck in a loop and alerts the team (alerts never cap spend)

ingest-to-kb.title: Getting documents into S3, and from S3 into the knowledge base

steps.label: DataSync copies the file share to S3 over TLS and verifies every file
Partners upload over SFTP; Transfer Family lands files in S3, restricted to their home directory
Each new object triggers an ingestion job, so the knowledge base stays current

global-delivery.title: Global delivery for a streaming chat API

steps.label: DNS (a latency or failover record) points users at CloudFront
Static assets come straight from the edge cache (GET and HEAD only)
API calls go to the origin: ALB, then ECS, then InvokeModelWithResponseStream
Tokens stream back. Every hop's timeout must outlast the model's longest pause
Partners that allow-list IPs use Global Accelerator's two static anycast addresses

ebs-efs.title: EBS is one server's disk; EFS is everyone's folder

steps.label: EBS: block storage attached to one instance in one Availability Zone, fast and private
EFS: one Regional file system mounted over NFS by many instances, containers and Lambda
EBS snapshots are never automatic (use DLM or AWS Backup) and restore into any AZ
